html:
The Ayoreo are an Indigenous people of the northern Gran Chaco, a dry forest and scrubland spanning Bolivia and Paraguay. They lived in small mobile groups, hunting, gathering honey and wild plants, and farming in the rainy season.

They stayed outside colonial and national control longer than almost anyone else in South America. The Chaco War between Bolivia and Paraguay was fought across their land from 1932 to 1935. From the 1940s onwards most Ayoreo groups were brought into missions, often after violent clashes. Some, among them groups of the Totobiegosode, still avoid all contact, the only uncontacted people in South America outside the Amazon. Cattle ranchers clearing the forest for pasture now threaten them. Their neighbours to the south include the Enlhet.
